pages.title: Palaeotragus
pages.text: Palaeotragus ($(o)Palaeotragus rouenii$()) is an extinct giraffid that lived in southeastern Europe and western Asia during the Late Miocene, first described from fossils found at Pikermi in Greece.$(br2)It belongs to a group of primitive giraffids that resembled large okapis, with long legs and a moderately long neck.$(br2)Its relatives ranged widely across Africa and Eurasia, and some survived into the Early Pleistocene.
